## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC22.F5] Emigh and Riley introduce relational power theory as a reader addition that rejects elite theory based on stand-alone elite characteristics and instead makes elites and nonelites mutually constitutive — dim: theme_position — reader: Rebecca Jean Emigh and Dylan Riley — theme-origin: reader_addition — theme: Relational power and elite/nonelite co-constitution — plan-theme-link: outside-spine — position: They propose replacing elite theory with a historically specified relational account in which elite positions arise through power relations connecting elites and nonelites — anchor: "elite theory needs to be recast as “relational power theory,” which emphasizes the mutual constitution of elites and nonelites through the power relations that connect them." — doc: em:QASWYLCG — confidence: high

sections_inspected: The Tradition of Elite Theory: From Pareto to Lachmann, pp. 6–17
The Relational Power of Elites and Nonelites, pp. 24–33
Elites, Nonelites, and Historical Change, pp. 34–39
scope_outcomes.criterion: A substantive, anchored interpretation by the citing reader of at least one supplied engagement theme, or an explicitly labeled reader addition, concerning class, closure, political capitalism, meaning, estates, bureaucracy, political organization, or related theoretical standpoints.
scope_outcomes.basis: The coauthored introduction substantively interprets Weberian power, legitimacy, bureaucracy, organizational domination, and ideational meaning, while proposing relational power theory and multidimensional power as reader additions.
limitations: The document is a single coauthored introduction, not a complete account of either author’s work.
It does not substantively address estates, status honour, political capitalism, imperialism, or tax-farming as distinct themes.
The source metadata gives 2024, while the printed copyright notice states 2025.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
